findings.finding: The plan adds a Bedrock IAM grant but does not specify whether Bedrock model invocation logging is enabled for the account/region. CloudTrail captures IAM-level calls (sts:AssumeRole) but does NOT capture the model prompt/response payload or per-invocation metadata; that requires an explicit Bedrock model invocation logging configuration (an S3 or CloudWatch Logs destination set via the Bedrock console/API). Without it, there is no audit trail to detect credential misuse — for example, if a container escape allows an attacker to invoke models against this role's grant, there is nothing in the observability stack that would surface it.
findings.location: Testing section; Scope section; infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf
scenarios: A container escape grants an adversary the instance role's Bedrock permissions; without invocation logging, unlimited model calls go undetected until the AWS bill arrives.
A misconfigured future policy change silently broadens the Bedrock grant; without invocation logging there is no per-call audit to review.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If the hop-limit=2 contingency fires, add an explicit access-posture declaration (e.g., a note in ADR 0046 or the contingency section) stating that the gerrit and opcert containers' new ability to call the Bedrock-enabled instance role is an accepted, bounded limitation — naming which containers gain what new capability — rather than leaving it implicit in the shared-trust argument.
evidence: Plan states: 'Raising the hop limit therefore widens reach to containers that are already inside the same trust boundary' — argues bounded, but does not declare the access class for gerrit/opcert on the Bedrock-enabled role.

The plan acknowledges the shared-bridge topology explicitly: 'gerrit, review-bot, and opcert already share one default bridge, and all three are first-party rebar components that already receive instance-role-derived secrets through the .env'.

Receiving a secret via .env (a static copy at boot) is a different capability than being able to directly assume the instance role and call Bedrock (or any other IAM-granted service) on-demand at container runtime.

ABSENCE: the contingency section names the bounded-exposure rationale but does not state 'the gerrit and opcert containers gaining IMDS access to the Bedrock-enabled role is accepted' as a declared posture with a rationale — the undeclared posture is the gap.
findings.finding: The hop-limit=2 contingency path grants IMDS reachability to all containers on the shared bridge (gerrit, opcert, review-bot), giving each container the ability to obtain instance-role credentials that now include the new `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant — but the plan does not declare the access posture for the gerrit and opcert containers on this extended credential scope.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Contingency, decided in advance' paragraph; also Scope: `infra/terraform/main.tf` metadata_options contingency
scenarios: If the hop-limit contingency fires, the Gerrit container (which receives untrusted git data and runs hooks) gains the ability to call bedrock:InvokeModel on any anthropic.claude-* model via the instance role — unintended LLM API consumption or exfiltration if Gerrit hooks are compromised.
A future story that adds a higher-privilege action to the instance role would silently widen to all three containers if the hop-limit was raised and never narrowed.
findings.suggested_fix: In the contingency block of the Approach section, add one sentence: 'Under the hop-limit=2 contingency, gerrit and opcert also gain the ability to obtain instance-role credentials that include the bedrock:InvokeModel grant; this is accepted because both containers are first-party, already receive instance-role-derived secrets, and the Bedrock grant is scoped to anthropic.claude-* only.' Then include this same sentence verbatim in the ADR 0046 exception entry the plan already requires.

findings.finding: The plan's Scope section specifies that `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` (new file) is the deliverable and that `iam.tf` is NOT modified — the single-owner contract's whole point. But the bedrock policy was in fact added directly to `iam.tf` (lines 202-247), not to a new `iam_s7.tf`. The plan's AC1 (`git diff --stat infra/terraform/iam.tf` shows no change) therefore describes an already-violated condition. A future executor reading the plan would expect to create `iam_s7.tf` and leave `iam.tf` unchanged, but would instead find the policy already in `iam.tf` with no `iam_s7.tf` file existing — a contradictory starting state that makes AC1 unachievable.
findings.location: Scope section ('infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf (new)') and AC1 ('git diff --stat infra/terraform/iam.tf shows no change')

findings.finding: The plan's Scope section declares 'infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf (new)' as the deliverable — following the iam_s2.tf/iam_s4a.tf single-story file convention the plan explicitly invokes — but the actual codebase shows the Bedrock policy was landed directly in iam.tf (lines 202-247) and iam_s7.tf does not exist. This directly violates the single-owner contract the plan itself cites (iam.tf:4-9: 'downstream stories must NOT edit iam.tf'), makes the plan's first AC ('git diff --stat infra/terraform/iam.tf shows no change') falsified by the as-landed code, and leaves the runbook citing the wrong owning file.

findings.finding: The plan's stated inference-profile resource ARN (`arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-*`) is both region-pinned and prefix-restricted to `us.`, which would silently deny `global.` inference profiles (e.g. `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) and any profile hosted in a non-us-east-1 region — the same cross-region routing the plan correctly wildcards for foundation-model ARNs. An implementer following the plan text exactly would produce an under-scoped policy that fails at runtime for a valid model id.
findings.location: Approach section — IAM grant resource ARNs: `arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-*`
findings.suggested_fix: Change the inference-profile ARN in the Approach section from `arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-*` to `arn:aws:bedrock:*:<account-id>:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`, matching the implemented code at `iam.tf:238` and the same cross-region-routing rationale already stated for foundation-model ARNs.

findings.finding: The grant of `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` for the streaming path is asserted by symmetry but never verified by a real call. The plan's own evidentiary standard states that only a real call (not the policy simulator) reveals which IAM action a service actually authorizes against — this was applied to the non-streaming Converse path but not to the ConverseStream path. If `ConverseStream` authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` rather than `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`, the streaming action grant is superfluous blast radius; if it authorizes against a third action entirely, streaming calls will fail in production even with this grant.
findings.location: Approach section — 'bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream'; Testing section — AC for real from-instance call; infra/terraform/iam.tf:234
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the runbook's step 2 with a streaming variant: `aws ssm send-command ... --parameters 'commands=["aws bedrock-runtime converse-stream --region us-east-1 --model-id us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 --messages ... 2>&1"]'` and add an AC: 'a real bedrock-runtime converse-stream call from the instance returns a model response, confirming InvokeModelWithResponseStream is the authorized action for the streaming path'.

findings.finding: The plan's Approach section states the inference-profile resource ARN as `arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-*` (region-pinned to us-east-1, prefix scoped to us. only), but the actual shipped HCL (iam.tf:238) uses `arn:aws:bedrock:*:${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*` (wildcard region, glob prefix capturing us., global., etc.). If a future operator uses the plan text as the authoritative spec to audit or re-implement the grant, they could apply the narrower ARN, which would break global. inference profiles and silently deny calls routed outside us-east-1.

findings.finding: The inference-profile IAM resource ARN stated in the plan text (`arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-*`) does not match the ARN actually implemented in `iam.tf` line 238 (`arn:aws:bedrock:*:${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`). Two specific differences: (1) the plan pins region `us-east-1` but the implementation wildcards the region to `*`; (2) the plan uses prefix `us.anthropic.claude-*` (matching only `us.*` cross-region profiles) while the implementation uses `*.anthropic.claude-*` (matching any regional prefix, e.g. `eu.`, `ap.`, `global.`).
